entries.title: The directional matrix norm is not its spectral radius
entries.locator: arXiv:1212.6390v1 (11 December 2012), (3.12)–(3.15), printed p.14 / PDF index13, and Theorem 3.5 proof, printed p.17 / PDF index16; also the 14 January 2012 author PDF, proof following Lemmas 3.6–3.7, printed p.18. Extracted text checked; journal and visual comparison unavailable.
entries.claim: The proof identifies the Euclidean operator norm of the directional matrix with the largest eigenvalue modulus.
entries.problem: This needs normality. On the hypercube the matrix is (C-I)D, with C all ones and D diagonal with entries +1 or -1. Its Euclidean norm is always m-1, since D is orthogonal. For m=3 and D=diag(-1,1,1), its eigenvalues are -1 and the two roots of r^2-r+2; the spectral radius is sqrt(2), strictly below the norm 2.
entries.correction: The scalar path-count recurrence gives separate edge- and middle-frequency estimates, including repeated roots. These prove the required two-time hypercube mixing bound directly. They do not establish the source's sharper coefficient-one Fourier estimate or all torus conclusions.
entries.leanImpact: A formal proof must not replace a nonnormal operator norm by eigenvalue moduli. The scalar recurrence is an alternative route for the hypercube mixing target. The sharper source estimate and general torus statements remain separate proof obligations.

resolution.summary: A direct recurrence proof recovers the hypercube mixing conclusion; the full scope of the original norm-based argument remains unresolved.
resolution.impact: The proof mechanism is replaced, not a constant or typographical symbol. The mixing conclusion needed here is preserved, but this is not a complete repair of every result using the original estimate.

versionAudit.method: The directional norm step and hypercube proof were compared in extracted text with the earlier dated author PDF. This summary consolidates the existing entry locators and reading records; it is not a fresh primary-text or visual-PDF audit.
versionAudit.scope: The single report is observed in both checked manuscripts. It does not establish a defect in the 2013 Journal of Statistical Physics edition, which has not been compared here. The scalar-recurrence workaround does not certify the sharper source bound. The report remains provisional.

comparisons.findings: The proof following Lemmas 3.6–3.7, p.18, uses the same norm/spectral-radius step as the December preprint. The January date is retained as printed; this is an earlier manuscript, not a later correction.
